Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Deptt. Lko And 3 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Dinesh Kumar Dixit,Vinay Mishra
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned Aga and perused the record.

2. The applicant seeks enlargement on bail in Fir No.0196 of 2024, under Section 363, 366, 376(2)n
of Ipc and Section 5(l)/6 of Pocso Act, P.S. Kaiserganj, District Bahraich.

entities.text: Pocso Act, P.S. Kaiserganj, District Bahraich
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3.  The FIR in question was lodged as a missing person report alleging that sister of the informant was enticed by the applicant.
Subsequently, in the two statements, the victim did not support the prosecution and accepted that both of them had gone to Delhi and Haryana.
There was slight variance in the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
The victim was also found to be positive for pregnancy.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant stated that the applicant is ready and willing to solemnize the Anil Yadav vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home ... on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32456943/
1 marriage as the relationship was consensual.

entities.text: Anil Yadav vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. Learned AGA has opposed the bail application.
6. Considering the two statements not supporting the prosecution, the applicant who is in custody since 21.07.2024 and has no criminal history, is entitled to be enlarged on bail.
In view thereof, the application is allowed.

7. Let the applicant Anil Yadav be released on bail in aforesaid FIR number on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
